content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"General is short of staff, not facing extra demand. It logged 6 absences against a usual 2.4: 2 called in sick, and 4 were sent home unwell by team leads between morning and 12:12. Agents on phones fell from about 33 to 27 against 33–38 planned, and service level dropped to 58% at 12:30. Volume today is near forecast (+4.7%), handle times are normal, no call reason is rising, there is no marketing entry, and the only incident (branch printers) does not affect the phones. Payments is broadly on plan for volume and staff, though it is running thin at 66.7% service level at 12:30.","plan_name":"General sick-wave cover: overtime plus coaching and break flex","rationale":"General is about 5–6 agents short for the rest of the day. Moving cross-skilled agents from payments is ruled out because payments is already below 70% service level and cannot donate. Delaying general breaks and cancelling general coaching recovers capacity straight away while overtime is arranged. Overtime starts at 13:15 because agents arrive 30 minutes after approval. Three consecutive 2-hour offers of 12 agents each should bring about 5 acceptances per block, at roughly Rs 3,600 per block and about Rs 10,800 in total, inside the Rs 15,000 budget.
